diagnose.label: Diagnosis
diagnose.title: Start with the bottleneck, not the tool.
diagnose.lead: A good-looking website, an ad campaign or an AI workflow is only worth something when it serves the actual business problem and leaves the company able to operate better.

items.title: Positioning is unclear
items.description: Customers cannot say why they should choose you over the alternative. Every media cost after that pays for the ambiguity.
items.symptom: Price is the only reason customers mention

items.title: Marketing runs in pieces
items.description: Content, advertising, the website, sales and data all run in parallel but never connect, so nobody sees the whole picture.
items.symptom: Each channel reports its own number and they never reconcile

items.title: Growth cannot be measured
items.description: There is plenty of activity but no tracking, no dashboard and no decision standard, so optimisation runs on instinct.
items.symptom: No answer to which spend produced revenue

items.title: AI & Data Strategy
items.problem: Data sits in several places and nobody uses it to decide anything. Reports exist to be filed, not to change course.
items.diagnosis: Before building a dashboard, you need to know which decisions the business actually makes, how often, and which number is missing to make them less of a guess.
items.methodology: Define the data set that must exist, standardise how it is measured, build the reporting layer around decisions, then put AI on the repeatable steps: summarising, classifying and alerting.
deliverables: Data map and shared metric definitions
GA4, GTM and pixel setup with data validation
Dashboards organised by decision, not by channel
AI workflows for research, synthesis and alerting

items.title: Brand & Positioning
items.problem: Customers have no clear reason to choose you, so every conversation returns to price.
items.diagnosis: Positioning is not a slogan. It answers who you serve, which problem you solve distinctly better, and what evidence proves it.
items.methodology: Research customers and competitors, settle the insight and USP, build the message architecture, then package it into a visual system and sales assets usable day to day.
deliverables: Sales asset set and a 90-day content plan

items.title: Growth Marketing
items.problem: Ad budget goes up and revenue does not follow, because the funnel leaks at steps nobody tracks.
items.diagnosis: Advertising amplifies a system, including its weaknesses. Find the step that loses the most people before spending more.
items.methodology: Build landing pages and the conversion flow, set up tracking you can trust, run campaigns as testable hypotheses, then optimise on a fixed cycle.
deliverables: Meta Ads and Google Ads campaign structure
An experiment system with evaluation standards

items.title: Marketing Operations
items.problem: Everything depends on a few people remembering. When they are away, quality drops.
items.diagnosis: Weak operations is rarely a lack of effort. It is the absence of process that can be written down, handed over and checked.
items.methodology: Standardise process and work states, build a management dashboard, automate the repeatable steps, then train and hand over to the internal team.
deliverables: Marketing process and CRM or lead workflow
Response SLA and handover standard between marketing and sales
Automation of repeatable tasks with n8n and scripts
Management dashboard, training and team handover

growthCheck.title: Growth Check
growthCheck.description: Twelve questions that show where the four growth pillars are strong and where they are weak. The result points at the priority bottleneck; it is not a score or a ranking.
growthCheck.scaleHint: 1 means nothing in place, 5 means standardised and measured

pillars.title: Positioning and messaging
questions: Customers can describe how you differ from competitors
The sales message is the same on every channel
There is concrete evidence behind the brand promise
pillars.recommend: Clarify positioning and message architecture before increasing media spend.
pillars.dontYet: Do not open another advertising channel.

pillars.title: Demand generation
questions: You know which channel brings real customers
Content exists for each step of the buying decision
Cost to acquire a customer is clearly calculated
pillars.recommend: Focus on one primary channel and build content for the whole journey before expanding.
pillars.dontYet: Do not run several campaigns in parallel.

pillars.title: Conversion and sales
questions: Every lead has an owner and a response deadline
Follow-up runs on a rhythm instead of one call
Reasons for losing a deal are recorded
pillars.recommend: Standardise lead intake, response SLA and the follow-up sequence.
pillars.dontYet: Do not increase lead volume while current leads are dropping.

pillars.title: Measurement and operations
questions: Website and advertising tracking is validated
A dashboard connects lead source to revenue
Process is written down and can be handed over
pillars.recommend: Build the measurement layer that links lead source to revenue before optimising deeper.
pillars.dontYet: Do not conclude which channel performs better.

calculators.title: ROAS
calculators.description: Revenue returned per unit of ad spend.
calculators.note: ROAS is before cost of goods. Read it next to break-even ROAS to know whether the number is enough.

calculators.title: Break-even ROAS
calculators.description: The minimum ROAS that avoids a loss, derived from gross margin.
calculators.note: Below this line, every unit of ad spend is taking profit away.

calculators.title: CAC
calculators.description: Cost to acquire one new customer.
calculators.note: Include people and tooling cost, not only media spend.

calculators.title: LTV
calculators.description: What a customer is worth across the time they stay.
calculators.note: An LTV to CAC ratio under 3 usually signals the model is not sustainable yet.

calculators.title: LTV / CAC ratio
calculators.description: The relationship between customer value and what it cost to win them.
calculators.note: Under 1 loses money per customer. Over 5 usually means growth is being left on the table.

hero.label: About
hero.title: Marketing does not start with advertising.
hero.lead: It starts with the product, the experience, trust, and the ability to turn data into better decisions.

body: DNGWORKS is the consulting practice of Dũng Nguyễn, working from Đà Nẵng with small and medium businesses in Vietnam. Most projects begin at the same place: the company has done plenty, but nobody can say which part is producing revenue.

The method is diagnosis before proposal. In practice the first sessions go into reading the data that already exists, listening to the sales team explain why deals were lost, and following the real customer journey rather than a funnel diagram on paper.

After diagnosis the work turns to system design: positioning and messaging, content and touchpoints, the conversion flow, the data layer, then automation of whatever repeats. A project is not finished when files are handed over. It is finished when the internal team can run the system without me.

items.title: Diagnose before quoting
items.description: The right scope only appears after the problem is understood. Quoting before diagnosis sells a solution to an unknown problem.

items.title: Every number traces to a source
items.description: Any metric in a report has to say where it came from, how it was measured and where the error sits. A number you cannot trace is not a number you decide with.

items.title: Hand over so the business can run it
items.description: A system that depends on the person who built it is unfinished. Process, documentation and training are in scope, not extras.

hero.label: DNG Intelligence
hero.title: Industry news, edited briefings and original analysis.
hero.lead: Tracking AI, advertising, e-commerce and business markets. Third-party stories always link back to the publisher; anything DNGWORKS writes is read in full here.

intelligence.externalNotice: This is a third-party story. DNGWORKS shows the headline, the source and a short excerpt; the rest is read at the original publisher.

sourcePolicy.title: Source policy
sourcePolicy.lead: How DNG Intelligence selects stories, handles rights and displays time.

sections.title: Three content types, never mixed
sections.body: Industry news is third-party content: the original headline, the source, the publication time and a short excerpt, with a link to the original. A DNG briefing is a short piece written by DNGWORKS from several cited sources. Analysis and playbooks are longer original work with method and examples. The three are always labelled separately and never presented as one another.

sections.title: No full-text copying
sections.body: DNGWORKS does not store, re-translate or republish anyone else's article in full. Excerpts are limited to what a reader needs in order to decide whether to open the original.

sections.title: Timestamps say what they are
sections.body: The publication time of the original and the time the system fetched the data are two different numbers and are displayed separately. When a source provides no publication time, the page says the date is unknown rather than guessing.

sections.title: Images
sections.body: Images are only used where the source permits reuse. Where no usable image exists, the page uses DNGWORKS editorial artwork and labels it as an illustration rather than a photograph of the event.

sections.title: Filtered on relevance, not on traffic
sections.body: Stories are scored on relevance to business, marketing, AI, technology and e-commerce. Entertainment, sport and other off-industry topics are excluded even when a source is pushing them hard.

sections.title: When a source fails
sections.body: The system keeps the most recent valid snapshot and states when it last synchronised, instead of showing an empty list or inventing replacement stories.
